records.claim: When nitrofurantoin was given to men at doses higher than typical for 2 weeks, sperm production was low or stopped in 13 out of the 36 study participants. Low sperm production could affect male fertility (ability to make healthy sperm). However, the use of typical doses of 100mg twice a day for 1 week did not have the same effect. This means that with typical use, nitrofurantoin is unlikely to affect male fertility. In general, exposures that men have are unlikely to increase risks to a pregnancy. For more information, please see the MotherToBaby fact sheet Paternal Exposures at https://mothertobaby.org/fact-sheets/paternal-exposures-pregnancy/.
records.source_section: If a man takes nitrofurantoin, could it affect his fertility or increase the chance of birth defects?
